noah: heads-up: onboarding sable-100k (int2-opt) into long-fuzz. hitting a tiny, reproducible kvcache index creep + RoPE phase mismatch around 52k tokens.
hana: int2-opt? that's new. does fp16/int4 reproduce?
noah: fp16 and int4v2 clean to 100k. int2-opt repro on GPU with batch=1. short sequences fine.
vik: can you paste repro command + small log?
noah: repro:
```
./ci/onboard_long.sh --model sable-100k --quant int2-opt --seq 60000 --batch 1 --seed 101 --mode fuzz
```
log snippet:
```
[kv] shard=1 read_pos=51999 expected_chunk=649 got_chunk=650
[rot] phase_accum ~ 51999.999 -> recompute 52000.001 delta=0.002
[token] emitted: "we" -> later emitted: "\n" at pos 52005
[perf] tok_latency: 156ms -> 188ms
```
samir: that read_pos->chunk mismatch + phase delta smells like index rounding due to reduced accumulator width on int2 path. int2-opt likely packs accumulators tightly.
hana: could be LUT interpolation too. int2 kernels often use ultra-cheap sin/cos approximations to save cycles. rounding error accumulates and pushes index boundary.
vik: is async eviction on?
noah: yes: KV_EVICT=async, KV_PREFETCH=on. turning off async moves event later but doesn't remove it.
hana: try ROPE_SCALE=1 and ROTARY_REEVAL_INTERVAL=1000. also try running with DEBUG_PHASE_CHECK=1 to emit cheap checksums every 512 tokens.
noah: did both. ROPE_SCALE=1 delayed failure to ~56k. REEVAL_INTERVAL=1k produced check-but-no-fix (checksum changed earlier). DEBUG_PHASE_CHECK shows checksum drift starting at ~51.8k.
debug-bot: incident created: IN-296123-SABLE-INT2-KV. run linked: 2961234567
ops-bot: snapshot saved s3://redwood-ci/sable/2961234567/snap.tgz (tags:int2-opt,long-fuzz)
vik: next steps proposal:
- vik to bisect int2-opt kernels scalar vs vector implementations
- hana to add cheap phase-guard that triggers renorm only when checksum delta exceeds threshold
- samir to add assertion in kvcache writer that records (shard,pos,checksum) on mismatch (no crash)
- noah to run golden fp16 plus matrix with eviction toggles
noah: quick bisect update: ran scalar-only int2 kernel and repro disappeared in 3/3 trials to 60k. vectorized int2 repros quickly. So likely a vector kernel race/packing rounding artefact.
vik: thanks. that's useful. vector path uses 8-bit lane packing with manual lane-shift writes; a single byte misalign can propagate. Can you enable SHARD_WRITE_SAFE=1 to force aligned writes?
noah: enabled SHARD_WRITE_SAFE=1: repro moves to ~61k but still appears eventually in long runs.
hana: if vector arithmetic rounding is root cause, maybe we should try mixed-precision accumulation only in the rotary compute path (FP32 accumulate, then quantize to int table) for long sequences. That mitigates accumulator drift while keeping packed writes for most work.
samir: agreed. also add periodic barrier before kvcache commit: compute a fast checksum and if it differs from reader checksum allow a short retry window where writer attempts a second write. Hopefully masks transient byte-tear.
noah: I ran a trial with ROTARY_MIXED_ACCUM=1 (FP32 accumulate) + SHARD_WRITE_SAFE=1 + DEBUG_PHASE_CHECK=1. result: no desync to 100k in 2/2 runs. Perf hit ~9% on throughput.
vik: good signal. Could be acceptable behind a runtime flag for sequences >32k. We should automate a matrix: quant=[int2-opt,int3,int4v2] x write_safe=[on,off] x accum=[on,off] x evict=[async,sync]. bench-bot?
ops-bot: bench job scheduled: 2961234567-matrix. results to s3://redwood-ci/sable/matrix/2961234567/
hana: low-cost guard idea: compute 8-lane rotary checksum every 1024 tokens; if delta>epsilon then enable mixed-accum dynamically for remainder of sequence. That way typical runs unaffected but we protect long drifters. I'll prototype.
vik: also add kernel logging for the vector path packing offsets (sampled) so we can see if a pattern of lane misalign happens before checksum flips. samir: I'll handle kvcache nonfatal dump and correlate checksums in snapshot.
noah: owners: vik (bisect + vector audit), hana (guard + dynamic mixed-accum), samir (kvcache dump + nonfatal assertion), noah (matrix runs + golden fp16).
samir: small ops note: add telemetry event "int2_rotary_correction" sampled 0.5% when guard triggers and save model+kernel+seq_len. ops says ok.
ops-bot: telemetry event added (sample_rate=0.5%)
oah: thanks team. will post matrix outputs when bench job completes. Also opening a hotfix PR to enable dynamic mixed-accum for seq>32k on int2 kernels behind runtime flag. PR link when ready. :thumbsup:
